sanskrit: divyo devapatho hy eṣa nātra gacchanti mānuṣāḥ yadartham āgataś cāsi tat saro 'bhyarṇa eva hi
english: This is the divine path of the gods; mortals do not travel here. The lake you have come for is quite near indeed.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ukto mahābāhur bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān praṇipatya tataḥ prītyā bhrātaraṃ hṛṣṭamānasaḥ uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā hanūmantaṃ kapīśvaram
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus addressed, the mighty-armed and valiant Bhimasena, having bowed with joy and gladness of heart, spoke gently to Hanuman, the lord of monkeys, calling him brother.

sanskrit: mayā dhanyataro nāsti yad āryaṃ dṛṣṭavān aham anugraho me sumahāṃs tṛptiś ca tava darśanāt
english: There is none more fortunate than I, for I have seen you, noble one. Your sight has bestowed on me a great blessing and deep satisfaction.

sanskrit: evaṃ tu kṛtam icchāmi tvayāryādya priyaṃ mama yat te tadāsīt plavataḥ sāgaraṃ makarālayam rūpam apratimaṃ vīra tad icchāmi nirīkṣitum
english: There is one favour I wish you to do for me now, noble one: that incomparable form you bore when you leaped across the ocean, the abode of sea-monsters — that form, O hero, I desire to behold.

sanskrit: evaṃ tuṣṭo bhaviṣyāmi śraddhāsyāmi ca te vacaḥ evam uktaḥ sa tejasvī prahasya harir abravīt
english: In that way I shall be fully satisfied and shall truly believe your words. Thus addressed, that radiant monkey laughed and spoke.

sanskrit: na tac chakyaṃ tvayā draṣṭuṃ rūpaṃ nānyena kena cit kālāvasthā tadā hy anyā vartate sā na sāṃpratam
english: That form cannot be seen by you, nor by anyone else; the condition of that time was different, and it does not obtain now.

sanskrit: anyaḥ kṛtayuge kālas tretāyāṃ dvāpare 'paraḥ ayaṃ pradhvaṃsanaḥ kālo nādya tad rūpam asti me
english: Time was one thing in the Krita age, another in the Treta, yet another in the Dvapara; this present age is one of deterioration — I no longer have that form.

sanskrit: bhūmir nadyo nagāḥ śailāḥ siddhā devā maharṣayaḥ kālaṃ samanuvartante yathā bhāvā yuge yuge balavarṣmaprabhāvā hi prahīyanty udbhavanti ca
english: The earth, rivers, trees, mountains, siddhas, gods, and great sages all follow the course of time; the conditions of existence in each age vary accordingly, and strength, stature, and power diminish and arise in turn.

sanskrit: tad alaṃ tava tad rūpaṃ draṣṭuṃ kurukulodvaha yugaṃ samanuvartāmi kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: So enough — let it be; you cannot see that form, O ornament of the Kuru line. I conform to the age, for time is impossible to transgress.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca yugasaṃkhyāṃ samācakṣva ācāraṃ ca yuge yuge dharmakāmārthabhāvāṃś ca varṣma vīryaṃ bhavābhavau
english: Bhima said: Describe to me the reckoning of the ages and the conduct in each age — the states of dharma, desire, and wealth, the stature, the strength, the rise and fall in each.

sanskrit: hanūmān uvāca kṛtaṃ nāma yugaṃ tāta yatra dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ kṛtam eva na kartavyaṃ tasmin kāle yugottame
english: Hanuman said: There is an age called Krita, dear one, in which eternal dharma prevails; in that supreme age, what is to be done is already done — no further effort is needed.

sanskrit: na tatra dharmāḥ sīdanti na kṣīyante ca vai prajāḥ tataḥ kṛtayugaṃ nāma kālena guṇatāṃ gatam
english: In it dharmas do not decline, nor do creatures diminish; and so, by virtue of its qualities, time has named it Krita.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvayakṣarākṣasapannagāḥ nāsan kṛtayuge tāta tadā na krayavikrayāḥ
english: In the Krita age, dear one, there were no gods, Danavas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Rakshasas, or serpents; and there was no buying and selling.

sanskrit: na sāmayajuṛgvarṇāḥ kriyā nāsīc ca mānavī abhidhyāya phalaṃ tatra dharmaḥ saṃnyāsa eva ca
english: There were no Sama, Yajur, or Rig Vedic ritual classes, nor any human rite; dharma there was simply meditation on the fruit and renunciation alone.

sanskrit: na tasmin yugasaṃsarge vyādhayo nendriyakṣayaḥ nāsūyā nāpi ruditaṃ na darpo nāpi paiśunam
english: In that confluence of ages there was no disease, no deterioration of the senses, no envy, no weeping, no arrogance, and no backbiting.

sanskrit: na vigrahaḥ kutas tandrī na dveṣo nāpi vaikṛtam na bhayaṃ na ca saṃtāpo na cerṣyā na ca matsaraḥ
english: There was no strife, how could there be sloth, no hatred, no perversity, no fear, no sorrow, no jealousy, and no envy.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramakaṃ brahma yā gatir yogināṃ parā ātmā ca sarvabhūtānāṃ śuklo nārāyaṇas tadā
english: Then the supreme Brahman — that highest goal of yogins and the self of all beings — Narayana was white (in that age).

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrāś ca kṛtalakṣaṇāḥ kṛte yuge samabhavan svakarmaniratāḥ prajāḥ
english: Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras, bearing the marks of the Krita age, were in that age creatures fully devoted to their own duties.

sanskrit: samāśramaṃ samācāraṃ samajñānamatībalam tadā hi samakarmāṇo varṇā dharmān avāpnuvan
english: With equal stages of life, equal conduct, equal knowledge and surpassing strength, the varnas, performing identical acts, attained to dharmas.

sanskrit: ekavedasamāyuktā ekamantravidhikriyāḥ pṛthagdharmās tv ekavedā dharmam ekam anuvratāḥ
english: United in one Veda, performing rites of one mantra and one rule, though having separate dharmas they adhered to one Veda and followed one dharma.

sanskrit: cāturāśramyayuktena karmaṇā kālayoginā akāmaphalasaṃyogāt prāpnuvanti parāṃ gatim
english: Through action united with the four stages of life, in harmony with time, without attachment to the fruit of desire, they attained the highest state.

sanskrit: ātmayogasamāyukto dharmo 'yaṃ kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ kṛte yuge catuṣpādaś cāturvarṇyasya śāśvataḥ
english: This dharma, marked by the Krita age's quality and united with self-yoga, was in the Krita age fourfold and eternal for the four varnas.

sanskrit: etat kṛtayugaṃ nāma traiguṇyaparivarjitam tretām api nibodha tvaṃ yasmin satraṃ pravartate
english: This is what is called the Krita age, free from the three qualities. Now learn about the Treta age as well, in which the great soma sacrifice proceeds.

sanskrit: pādena hrasate dharmo raktatāṃ yāti cācyutaḥ satyapravṛttāś ca narāḥ kriyādharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: By one quarter dharma diminishes; Achyuta (Vishnu) takes on a reddish hue; and men, bent on truth, are devoted to ritual and dharma.

sanskrit: tato yajñāḥ pravartante dharmāś ca vividhāḥ kriyāḥ tretāyāṃ bhāvasaṃkalpāḥ kriyādānaphalodayāḥ
english: Then sacrifices come into being, and various dharmic rites; in the Treta intentions and resolutions arise, and the fruits of ritual action and giving.

sanskrit: pracalanti na vai dharmāt tapodānaparāyaṇāḥ svadharmasthāḥ kriyāvanto janās tretāyuge 'bhavan
english: Devoted to austerity and giving, they do not swerve from dharma; people in the Treta age abided in their own duty and were active in religious observance.

sanskrit: dvāpare 'pi yuge dharmo dvibhāgonaḥ pravartate viṣṇur vai pītatāṃ yāti caturdhā veda eva ca
english: In the Dvapara age too, dharma proceeds diminished by two quarters; Vishnu takes on a yellow hue, and the Veda is divided fourfold.

sanskrit: tato 'nye ca caturvedās trivedāś ca tathāpare dvivedāś caikavedāś cāpy anṛcaś ca tathāpare
english: Then some know all four Vedas, others three, others two, others one; and yet others have no Vedic knowledge at all.

sanskrit: evaṃ śāstreṣu bhinneṣu bahudhā nīyate kriyā tapodānapravṛttā ca rājasī bhavati prajā
english: With the sacred texts thus divided, rites are conducted in many ways; people become passionate and oriented toward austerity and giving.

sanskrit: ekavedasya cājñānād vedās te bahavaḥ kṛtāḥ satyasya ceha vibhraṃśāt satye kaś cid avasthitaḥ
english: Because of the ignorance of the one Veda, many Vedas were made; and due to the decay of truth here, only a few remain established in truth.

sanskrit: satyāt pracyavamānānāṃ vyādhayo bahavo 'bhavan kāmāś copadravāś caiva tadā daivatakāritāḥ
english: For those who fall away from truth, many diseases arise, and desires and afflictions come, caused then by the gods.

sanskrit: yair ardyamānāḥ subhṛśaṃ tapas tapyanti mānavāḥ kāmakāmāḥ svargakāmā yajñāṃs tanvanti cāpare
english: Tormented greatly by these, men perform austerities; some, desiring enjoyment, others desiring heaven, spread out sacrifices.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvāparam āsādya prajāḥ kṣīyanty adharmataḥ pādenaikena kaunteya dharmaḥ kaliyuge sthitaḥ
english: Thus, having entered the Dvapara, creatures decay through adharma; in the Kali age, O son of Kunti, dharma stands on one quarter alone.

sanskrit: tāmasaṃ yugam āsādya kṛṣṇo bhavati keśavaḥ vedācārāḥ praśāmyanti dharmayajñakriyās tathā
english: Having arrived at the dark age, Keshava becomes black; Vedic practices subside, and dharmic rites and sacrificial acts likewise.

sanskrit: ītayo vyādhayas tandrī doṣāḥ krodhādayas tathā upadravāś ca vartante ādhayo vyādhayas tathā
english: Calamities, diseases, sloth, faults such as anger, afflictions, mental anguish, and physical ailments come to prevail.

sanskrit: yugeṣv āvartamāneṣu dharmo vyāvartate punaḥ dharme vyāvartamāne tu loko vyāvartate punaḥ
english: As the ages revolve, dharma revolves again; as dharma revolves, the world revolves again.

sanskrit: loke kṣīṇe kṣayaṃ yānti bhāvā lokapravartakāḥ yugakṣayakṛtā dharmāḥ prārthanāni vikurvate
english: When the world is exhausted, the forces that set the world in motion decay; dharmas created by the decay of ages distort their own aspirations.

sanskrit: etat kaliyugaṃ nāma acirād yat pravartate yugānuvartanaṃ tv etat kurvanti cirajīvinaḥ
english: This is what is called the Kali age, which before long comes into force; those who live long keep following this succession of ages.

sanskrit: yac ca te matparijñāne kautūhalam ariṃdama anarthakeṣu ko bhāvaḥ puruṣasya vijānataḥ
english: And your curiosity about knowing me — what attachment should a wise man have to things of no ultimate purpose, O subduer of enemies?

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi yugasaṃkhyāṃ mahābāho svasti prāpnuhi gamyatām
english: All of what you asked me — the reckoning of the ages — has been told to you. Now fare you well, O mighty-armed one; go on your way.

sanskrit: bhīma uvāca pūrvarūpam adṛṣṭvā te na yāsyāmi kathaṃ cana yadi te 'ham anugrāhyo darśayātmānam ātmanā
english: Bhima said: Without seeing your former form I shall not depart in any way. If you would favour me, reveal yourself by yourself.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu bhīmena smitaṃ kṛtvā plavaṃgamaḥ tad rūpaṃ darśayām āsa yad vai sāgaralaṅghane
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus addressed by Bhima, the monkey smiled and displayed that form he had worn when leaping across the ocean.

sanskrit: bhrātuḥ priyam abhīpsan vai cakāra sumahad vapuḥ dehas tasya tato 'tīva vardhaty āyāmavistaraiḥ
english: Wishing to please his brother, he assumed a mighty body; his frame then grew exceedingly in length and breadth.

sanskrit: tad rūpaṃ kadalīṣaṇḍaṃ chādayann amitadyutiḥ gireś cocchrayam āgamya tasthau tatra sa vānaraḥ
english: Of immeasurable radiance, covering a grove of plantain trees with that form, the monkey rose to the height of a mountain and stood there.

sanskrit: samucchritamahākāyo dvitīya iva parvataḥ tāmrekṣaṇas tīkṣṇadaṃṣṭro bhṛkuṭīkṛtalocanaḥ dīrghalāṅgūlam āvidhya diśo vyāpya sthitaḥ kapiḥ
english: Rearing his immense body like a second mountain, with copper-red eyes, sharp fangs, and furrowed brows, the monkey swung his great tail and stood pervading all directions.

sanskrit: tad rūpaṃ mahad ālakṣya bhrātuḥ kauravanandanaḥ visismiye tadā bhīmo jahṛṣe ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Beholding that vast form of his brother, Bhima, the joy of the Kurus, was filled with wonder and thrilled again and again.

sanskrit: tam arkam iva tejobhiḥ sauvarṇam iva parvatam pradīptam iva cākāśaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmo nyamīlayat
english: Seeing him blazing like the sun with his radiance, like a golden mountain, like the sky on fire, Bhima closed his eyes.

sanskrit: ābabhāṣe ca hanumān bhīmasenaṃ smayann iva etāvad iha śaktas tvaṃ rūpaṃ draṣṭuṃ mamānagha
english: And Hanuman, smiling, spoke to Bhimasena: "This much of my form are you able to behold here, O sinless one."

sanskrit: vardhe 'haṃ cāpy ato bhūyo yāvan me manasepsitam bhīma śatruṣu cātyarthaṃ vardhate mūrtir ojasā
english: "I can grow still further, as much as my mind desires; and against enemies, Bhima, my form grows exceedingly with vigour."

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ mahāraudraṃ vindhyamandarasaṃnibham dṛṣṭvā hanūmato varṣma saṃbhrāntaḥ pavanātmajaḥ
english: Beholding that wonderful, tremendously terrible frame of Hanuman, like the Vindhya and Mandara mountains, the son of the wind was bewildered.

sanskrit: pratyuvāca tato bhīmaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ kṛtāñjalir adīnātmā hanūmantam avasthitam
english: Then Bhima, his body hair standing up in joy, replied to Hanuman who stood before him, with folded hands, his spirit undaunted.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaṃ pramāṇaṃ vipulaṃ śarīrasyāsya te vibho saṃharasva mahāvīrya svayam ātmānam ātmanā
english: "The vast measure of your body has been seen, O lord; now, O greatly valiant one, withdraw yourself into yourself."

sanskrit: na hi śaknomi tvāṃ draṣṭuṃ divākaram ivoditam aprameyam anādhṛṣyaṃ mainākam iva parvatam
english: "For I cannot look at you, risen like the sun, immeasurable and unapproachable, like the mountain Mainaka."

sanskrit: vismayaś caiva me vīra sumahān manaso 'dya vai yad rāmas tvayi pārśvasthe svayaṃ rāvaṇam abhyagāt
english: "And I have great wonder in my mind today, O hero, that with you at his side Rama himself went against Ravana."

sanskrit: tvam eva śaktas tāṃ laṅkāṃ sayodhāṃ sahavāhanām svabāhubalam āśritya vināśayitum ojasā
english: "You alone were capable of destroying that Lanka with all its warriors and vehicles, relying on your own arm's strength and vigour."

sanskrit: na hi te kiṃ cid aprāpyaṃ mārutātmaja vidyate tava naikasya paryāpto rāvaṇaḥ sagaṇo yudhi
english: "For there is nothing unattainable for you, O son of the wind; Ravana with all his forces was not a match for you alone in battle."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhīmena hanūmān plavagarṣabhaḥ pratyuvāca tato vākyaṃ snigdhagambhīrayā girā
english: Thus addressed by Bhima, Hanuman, the bull among monkeys, then replied with a voice gentle and deep.

sanskrit: evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi bhārata bhīmasena na paryāpto mamāsau rākṣasādhamaḥ
english: "It is so, great-armed one, as you say, O Bharata; Bhimasena, that vile Rakshasa was no match for me."

sanskrit: mayā tu tasmin nihate rāvaṇe lokakaṇṭake kīrtir naśyed rāghavasya tata etad upekṣitam
english: "But had I slain that thorn of the world, Ravana, the glory of Rama would have been lost; therefore I refrained."

sanskrit: tena vīreṇa hatvā tu sagaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam ānītā svapuraṃ sītā loke kīrtiś ca sthāpitā
english: "By that hero, having slain the lord of Rakshasas with all his forces, Sita was brought back to his city and his glory was established in the world."

sanskrit: tad gaccha vipulaprajña bhrātuḥ priyahite rataḥ ariṣṭaṃ kṣemam adhvānaṃ vāyunā parirakṣitaḥ
english: "So go now, O man of vast wisdom, devoted to your brother's welfare and happiness; may the path be free of ill and safe, protected by the wind."

sanskrit: eṣa panthāḥ kuruśreṣṭha saugandhikavanāya te drakṣyase dhanadodyānaṃ rakṣitaṃ yakṣarākṣasaiḥ
english: "This is the path, O best of Kurus, to the Saugandhika forest; you will see the garden of Kubera guarded by Yakshas and Rakshasas."

sanskrit: na ca te tarasā kāryaḥ kusumāvacayaḥ svayam daivatāni hi mānyāni puruṣeṇa viśeṣataḥ
english: "Do not by force gather the flowers yourself; the gods are to be especially honoured by a man."

sanskrit: balihomanamaskārair mantraiś ca bharatarṣabha daivatāni prasādaṃ hi bhaktyā kurvanti bhārata
english: "By offerings, oblations, salutations, and mantras, O bull of the Bharatas, the gods in their grace act with devotion, O Bharata."

sanskrit: mā tāta sāhasaṃ kārṣīḥ svadharmam anupālaya svadharmasthaḥ paraṃ dharmaṃ budhyasvāgamayasva ca
english: "Do not act rashly, dear one; uphold your own dharma. Established in your own dharma, understand the highest dharma and approach it."

sanskrit: na hi dharmam avijñāya vṛddhān anupasevya ca dharmo vai vedituṃ śakyo bṛhaspatisamair api
english: "Without knowing dharma, and without attending on the elders, dharma cannot truly be understood — not even by those equal to Brihaspati."

sanskrit: adharmo yatra dharmākhyo dharmaś cādharmasaṃjñitaḥ vijñātavyo vibhāgena yatra muhyanty abuddhayaḥ
english: "Where adharma goes by the name of dharma and dharma is called adharma — that distinction must be discerned carefully, where the unintelligent are confused."

sanskrit: ācārasaṃbhavo dharmo dharmād vedāḥ samutthitāḥ vedair yajñāḥ samutpannā yajñair devāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ
english: "Dharma is born of conduct; from dharma the Vedas arise; from the Vedas sacrifices are produced; by sacrifices the gods are established."

sanskrit: vedācāravidhānoktair yajñair dhāryanti devatāḥ bṛhaspatyuśanoktaiś ca nayair dhāryanti mānavāḥ
english: "The gods are sustained by sacrifices enjoined by Vedic conduct and rule; men are sustained by the policies declared by Brihaspati and Ushanas."

sanskrit: paṇyākaravaṇijyābhiḥ kṛṣyātho yonipoṣaṇaiḥ vārtayā dhāryate sarvaṃ dharmair etair dvijātibhiḥ
english: "By trade, mining, commerce, agriculture, and by the support of one's source of livelihood — by this economic activity and by these dharmas of the twice-born all is sustained."

sanskrit: trayī vārtā daṇḍanītis tisro vidyā vijānatām tābhiḥ samyakprayuktābhir lokayātrā vidhīyate
english: "The three Vedas, economics, and statecraft — these are the three branches of knowledge for the wise; when properly applied together, the journey of the world is ordered."

sanskrit: sā ced dharmakriyā na syāt trayīdharmam ṛte bhuvi daṇḍanītim ṛte cāpi nirmaryādam idaṃ bhavet
english: "If these dharmic activities were absent, if the triple Veda were absent from the earth, and if statecraft were absent too, this world would be without limit or restraint."

sanskrit: vārtādharme hy avartantyo vinaśyeyur imāḥ prajāḥ supravṛttais tribhir hy etair dharmaiḥ sūyanti vai prajāḥ
english: "Not following the dharma of livelihood, these people would perish; with these three dharmas well pursued, creatures truly flourish."

sanskrit: dvijānām amṛtaṃ dharmo hy ekaś caivaikavarṇikaḥ yajñādhyayanadānāni trayaḥ sādhāraṇāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: "For the twice-born, dharma is immortal; there is one dharma peculiar to each varna; sacrifice, study, and giving — these three are remembered as common to all."

sanskrit: yājanādhyāpane cobhe brāhmaṇānāṃ pratigrahaḥ pālanaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ vai vaiśyadharmaś ca poṣaṇam
english: "Both officiating at rites and teaching, as well as receiving gifts, are for Brahmanas; protection is for Kshatriyas; the dharma of Vaishyas is nurturing."

sanskrit: śuśrūṣā tu dvijātīnāṃ śūdrāṇāṃ dharma ucyate bhaikṣahomavratair hīnās tathaiva guruvāsinām
english: "Service to the twice-born is said to be the dharma of Shudras; likewise those who lack begging, fire-offerings, and vows — the duty of those who live at the guru's house."

sanskrit: kṣatradharmo 'tra kaunteya tava dharmābhirakṣaṇam svadharmaṃ pratipadyasva vinīto niyatendriyaḥ
english: "The Kshatriya dharma here, O son of Kunti, is the protection of dharma; take up your own dharma, with humility and controlled senses."

sanskrit: vṛddhaiḥ saṃmantrya sadbhiś ca buddhimadbhiḥ śrutānvitaiḥ susthitaḥ śāsti daṇḍena vyasanī paribhūyate
english: "Having taken counsel with the aged, the righteous, the wise, and those versed in scripture, one who is well established rules through the rod of chastisement; the self-indulgent is overwhelmed."

sanskrit: nigrahānugrahaiḥ samyag yadā rājā pravartate tadā bhavati lokasya maryādā suvyavasthitā
english: "When a king properly exercises both punishment and favour, then the boundaries of the world are well and truly established."

sanskrit: tasmād deśe ca durge ca śatrumitrabaleṣu ca nityaṃ cāreṇa boddhavyaṃ sthānaṃ vṛddhiḥ kṣayas tathā
english: "Therefore, regarding territory, fortresses, and the strength of enemies and allies, one must always be alert through spies to one's position, growth, and decline."
